Vals native rerun with an eroding host contact surface (vp5)

Same 20-ply Vals native deck as vp4 (ball 1000 m/s, 70 µs). Change: the ball contacts the host through an element-based surface (EMBMESH_PLATE_ELEMS) that erodes with deleted elements, instead of node-based contact on every host node at 0.635 mm thickness; *Contact Output added so interface damage (CSDMG) is recorded. ROAR job 56651971, directory ctv/vp5/vals_native_erode, completed with exit code 0.

Summary

  • The kinetic-energy blow-up is gone. ALLKE peaks only 6.8% above the 3.55 J the ball starts with (vp4: +73%). ETOTAL still ends 7.9% above its start (vp4 ended -17% below), so the balance is still not closed; it is off by a smaller amount but in the other direction. The dissipated and stored energies are tiny (55 and 33 mJ for ALLIE and ALLDMD), so the plate absorbs almost nothing.
  • Delamination is now recorded. 1,796 interface contact points have failed and 13,930 are past half damage by 70 µs. Damage starts at about 7 µs and grows through the run.
  • Host deletion rose, not fell: 1,351 hosts deleted against 517 in vp4. Most of this comes in the first 44 µs. A plausible cause is that deleted elements no longer carry contact, so the ball pushes further in; I have not tested it.
  • Fibers rarely fail: 70 of 206,930 fiber elements deleted.
  • The ball erodes heavily: 3,161 of 18,500 ball elements (17%) are deleted, and the surviving ball elements stretch into spikes (see the renders). Ball erosion was not counted in vp4, so the comparison is host-only.

Caveats

  • The viewer export keeps only 200 frames and does not carry fiber or ball deletion state, so the renders show deleted host elements removed and fibers undeleted.
  • The ball node-median velocity stays at about -1000 m/s in both runs: the ball is barely slowed by the plate. I have not established why (the plate removes under 2% of its elements).
  • Ball elements stretch to long spikes as neighbouring elements erode; the ball velocity is a node median and should be read as approximate.
  • Only the contact surface changed between vp4 and vp5. The cohesive card (K 60 N/mm³, 1.8 MPa shear) is the unfixed base version.
  • Interactive movies: python agents/drafter/outbox/T-021/serve_viewer.py Meshing/vals-plywise-erode/results/viewer_vp5 --port 8820. The symmetry button now frames the plate and looks at the cut face from outside.
